docs/building-programs.md::Magistrate's.claim: garrison emphasis knob - the-main-gate-and-its-gatekeepers-nagaya-mon: the Kaibara jin'ya's ordinary gate range held a store of arms (the record names it a gun store; the map and its pop-ups label it a store of arms and name no firearm - the session's ruling of 2026-11-22 on how the store is labeled (feature 449 T265), not a recorded deviation: the GM's setting notes say nothing of firearms, so it takes the easier route where they are silent and contradicts no note); and the-magistrates-manor-in-a-town-where-it-stands-and-which-way-it-faces-jinya-and-yamen: Pingyao, with no standing barracks, kept its armory in the great hall's west end bay; Jiexiu's great hall's end bays held its gunpowder and weapons from 1591, and its account after 1677 lists an armory (武庫) on the east, inside the side gates, its words leaving open whether it stood there or west of a pavilion and whether it was a building or a room; at Nirayama the weapons store (武器庫) is a building of its own from late in the Edo period, and at Hamamashike, finished 1860, a weapons store (武器蔵) is named among the storehouses - every seat draws an armory at one of three sites, a knob rolled from the map's seed among the sites the sheet offers (the round arbiter's ask:armory-store-ubame, route (a), 2026-11-22; `armory_site`, feature 449 T303): the gate range where the main gate is drawn as one, the office hall's west end bay, or a store of its own, so a one-bay gate's sheet rolls between the hall's bay and a store; every pool sheet draws its armory where its seed rolls it - Ubame the gate range's west room (the-main-gate-and-its-gatekeepers-nagaya-mon.drawing), Hayakawa, Ochiba, the Ochiba round trip and the county example the hall's bay (feature 449 T276, measured 2026-11-22); bandit country adds ashigaru (a larger barracks) and a watchtower, and a quiet county keeps a token watch (the barracks at the knob's low end), all GUESSES, the record silent (feature 417 T33)
docs/building-programs.md::Magistrate's.note: the armory takes one of three attested sites (the gate range, the hall's west end bay, a store of its own) by a seeded roll, with a one-bay gate offered only the bay or the store, as 0093's drawing page draws it; the bandit and quiet-county additions are labeled guesses

rust/phases/src/waterward.rs::pieces#the.claim: the strip stops at the channel's bank - reed-beds-and-the-marshs-edge-yoshihara.drawing: its section "How our maps draw the marsh's edge" - where a stream or a ditch crosses the marsh the reeds are drawn right to the water's edge, and kept out of the water itself - each reach's bed taken out along its own sides at its drawn width, slanting or square; the strip ends at the bank of the channel that crosses the dike at a sluice (polders-fields-diked-against-the-fluctuating-water-weitian-waju.drawing: water crosses the dike only at gated sluices; polder-dikes-what-they-were-made-of-how-big-and-what-grew-on-them.drawing: where a channel crosses the dike the band is cut), so no reed is drawn across the channel the sluice shuts
